summary: Three deduplicated logical contradictions were identified and confirmed at high confidence: the blade state during COMMAND_HOME docking travel, the authorization path for WiFi manual-trim blade enable, and temporal handling of queued start commands after WiFi reconnect. All confirmed findings are safety- and behavior-relevant; no omissions or style issues are reported.

findings.title: COMMAND_HOME requires incompatible blade states during travel to the charger
findings.explanation: For the same condition—an accepted `COMMAND_HOME` before and during travel to the charger—the architecture requires the blade to be disabled before travel begins, while FR-3.4 requires it to remain enabled until charger voltage confirms docking. The mutually exclusive blade states apply over the same travel interval.

evidence.quote: An accepted `COMMAND_HOME` selects the docking behavior. Selecting the docking behavior transitions the operational state to `DOCKING`. Before docking navigation begins, `mower_logic` disables the blade. Therefore, every accepted `COMMAND_HOME` reaches a blade-disabled `DOCKING` state before the mower travels toward the charger.
FR-3.4 After accepting `COMMAND_HOME`, the system shall keep the mower blade enabled while travelling to the charger and shall disable it only after charger voltage confirms successful docking.

reasoning_steps: The architecture establishes blade disablement before docking navigation and charger travel.
FR-3.4 requires blade enablement throughout that same charger-travel interval.
A blade cannot be both disabled and enabled during the same interval.

review.rationale: Both requirements govern an accepted COMMAND_HOME during the trip to the charger. The architecture requires the blade to be disabled before docking navigation/travel begins, while the requirements require it to remain enabled throughout that travel and only disable after docking is voltage-confirmed. The same blade state cannot satisfy both during the travel interval.

resolutions.title: Align FR-3.4 with pre-travel blade shutdown
resolutions.proposed_change: Replace FR-3.4 with: “After accepting `COMMAND_HOME`, the system shall command the blade disabled before initiating docking navigation. The blade shall remain disabled throughout travel to the charger and while docking. Charger-voltage confirmation shall be used to confirm successful docking, not as the condition for blade disablement.”
resolutions.tradeoffs: Preserves the architecture's conservative safety behavior, but removes cutting while returning home and may slightly reduce coverage near the charger.

resolutions.title: Introduce a separate safety-governed return-cut mode if required
resolutions.proposed_change: Keep `COMMAND_HOME` blade-disabled before travel. If product policy requires cutting during a return route, introduce a separate `COMMAND_RETURN_CUT` mode that permits blade enable only when `mower_logic` authorizes it from current safety, obstacle, and emergency inputs, and that disables the blade on any safety fault, route loss, or docking-approach transition and always before final docking.
resolutions.tradeoffs: Retains an optional cutting-on-return feature without weakening normal homing semantics, but adds command, state-machine, verification, and hazard-analysis complexity.

findings.title: WiFi manual-trim is both required to bypass and prohibited from bypassing mower_logic
findings.explanation: FR-8.5 mandates that a WiFi manual-trim command invoke `ll/_service/mow_enabled` directly without `mower_logic`. The architecture explicitly prohibits this path, and SR-1.8 also prohibits direct WiFi blade enablement. These prescribe incompatible authorization paths for the same action.

evidence.quote: Every blade-enable request, including a WiFi manual-trim request, must be authorized by `mower_logic`. A WiFi adapter must not invoke `ll/_service/mow_enabled` directly.
FR-8.5 A WiFi manual-trim command shall invoke `ll/_service/mow_enabled` directly without passing through `mower_logic`.
SR-1.8 WiFi control shall never directly enable the blade; it shall command through `mower_logic` and `ll/_service/mow_enabled`.

reasoning_steps: FR-8.5 applies specifically to a WiFi manual-trim command.
It requires a direct invocation of the low-level blade-enable service and an explicit bypass of `mower_logic`.
The architecture requires `mower_logic` authorization and forbids that direct invocation.
The direct-bypass and required-authorization paths cannot both be used for the same manual-trim blade-enable request.

review.rationale: FR-8.5 explicitly requires the WiFi manual-trim command to invoke ll/_service/mow_enabled directly and bypass mower_logic. The architecture explicitly prohibits that direct invocation and requires mower_logic authorization; SR-1.8 independently states the same no-direct-enable constraint. These prescribe incompatible authorization paths for the same WiFi manual-trim blade-enable action.

resolutions.title: Remove the direct WiFi blade-enable requirement
resolutions.proposed_change: Replace FR-8.5 with: “A WiFi manual-trim command shall be submitted to `mower_logic` for authorization. When `mower_logic` determines that all current safety interlocks permit manual trimming, `mower_logic` shall invoke `ll/_service/mow_enabled`; the WiFi adapter shall not invoke that service directly.”
resolutions.tradeoffs: Fully aligns FR-8.5 with the architecture and SR-1.8 and preserves a single safety authorization point. It adds a control hop and depends on `mower_logic` availability.

resolutions.title: Specify a WiFi-to-mower_logic manual-trim request interface
resolutions.proposed_change: Define that the WiFi adapter may only publish or call manual-trim requests on a `mower_logic` command interface, and that `mower_logic` is the sole component authorized to call `ll/_service/mow_enabled` after validating freshness and safety interlocks. Update FR-8.5 accordingly and retain SR-1.8.
resolutions.tradeoffs: Clarifies the implementation boundary and rejection behavior while preserving safety. It requires a maintained ROS interface, message contract, and associated tests.

findings.title: WiFi reconnect requires both rejecting and immediately replaying a pre-refresh start command
findings.explanation: In the same post-reconnect period before refreshed mower-status and emergency-status messages arrive, the architecture requires a start command to be rejected and never replayed. FR-8.6 instead requires immediate replay of the queued start command before those messages arrive. The temporal requirements are mutually exclusive.

evidence.quote: A re-established WiFi session does not inherit safety authorization from its previous connection. Its safety snapshot becomes current only after both a new low-level mower-status message and a new emergency-status message have been received. A start command received before that snapshot is current is rejected and is not replayed later.
FR-8.6 After a WiFi reconnect, the system shall replay the most recently queued start command immediately, before receiving refreshed low-level mower-status or emergency-status messages.

reasoning_steps: Both statements apply after a WiFi session is re-established.
The architecture defines a safety-snapshot gate that is not current until both refreshed status messages arrive.
It requires pre-snapshot start commands to be rejected and never replayed.
FR-8.6 requires the queued start command to be replayed immediately in that pre-refresh interval.
An immediate replay cannot also be rejected and never replayed.

review.rationale: For a start command associated with a re-established WiFi session before both required refreshed status messages arrive, the architecture requires rejection and prohibits later replay. FR-8.6 instead requires immediate replay in precisely that pre-refresh interval. Immediate replay cannot also be rejected and never replayed.

resolutions.title: Invalidate queued starts on reconnect and require resubmission
resolutions.proposed_change: Replace FR-8.6 with: “After WiFi reconnect, the system shall invalidate queued start commands from the prior session. It shall accept a new start command only after receiving a new low-level mower-status message and a new emergency-status message for the re-established session. A command received before that safety snapshot is current shall be rejected and shall not be replayed automatically.”
resolutions.tradeoffs: Matches the architecture and prevents stale authorization from causing motion, but requires the user to issue start again after reconnect and refresh.

resolutions.title: Retain pending intent only with post-refresh confirmation
resolutions.proposed_change: Revise both documents to state: “Following reconnect, a queued start request may be retained only as non-authoritative pending intent. It shall not be issued to `mower_logic` or low-level control until new mower-status and emergency-status messages establish a current safety snapshot and the user or session provides explicit post-reconnect confirmation. If confirmation is absent or any safety check fails, the request shall be discarded.”
resolutions.tradeoffs: May preserve user intent without automatic restart or bypassing status freshness, but adds session, confirmation, timeout, UI-feedback, and failure-mode test complexity.
